decisions.text: arranged: rows by province or territory: no comparison within a panel is stated (facts.compare): one series per panel, the most panels and the least clutter (13-15 DP-1); 12 panels are stacked in rows (more than 6 across would be too narrow); runner-up for review: series in each panel by province or territory (D-38 (i))
one colour for every mark: every variable is on the rows or columns (G7.50)
type line: a regular series whose pattern of change is the point (06 DP6-1, G1.51)
one shared scale: one scale for every panel, so that sizes compare across panels (G7.48)
the values are not far from zero compared with their spread
scale 0–200 by 100 (at most 3 intervals in a panel about 30 pt high)
no point markers: no value is isolated and no straight run hides one
the unit's description on its own line above the scale (inline it would meet the line of ontario): “orders per month”; “200” stays on the top label
time axis: row 2 (“2022”) left out, the title gives it (G2.37)
12 × 1 panels of equal size, abutting, divided by light separators, no box round a panel (G7.51); each 248 pt wide and 30 pt high

scale labels left of the first column, the unit phrase once on the first row's top label and the other rows' top labels keeping the number's currency and magnitude; time labels only under the bottom row; row headers at the left, horizontal (G7.49)

findings.message: facts.compare not given: say which dims the insight compares directly, so that their series share a panel (G1.19)
findings.title: the series the insight compares directly share a panel

source.shows: a stack of small line charts for series that cross too often for one chart (R6-36): twelve panels, more than fit across, so stacked in rows, one series each, on one shared scale that shows which province is larger (R6-37, G7.48); the names at the left, the months only under the last panel, light separators; synthetic data after the book's figure, which does not name its measure
